question: For chapter 10 (Failure handling), does the three-category structure (mechanical / quality / strategic) fit best as three sequential SingleTrack instances, a three-column TrackDiagram variant, or a new stacked layout? What component shape keeps the diagram self-contained without exceeding the ~13-diagram cap?
findings: Three sequential SingleTrack instances is ruled out on semantic grounds: SingleTrack.astro (site/src/components/SingleTrack.astro, lines 9–45) is a single-column pipeline container fixed at max-width: 360px that encodes a sequential step progression via StepRow + StepArrow children. The three failure categories (mechanical / quality / strategic) are parallel classifications each with a distinct response shape — auto-retry, bounce-once-then-escalate, immediate-escalate — not ordered pipeline stages. Rendering them as three separate pipeline strips would imply sequence and consume 3 diagram slots, bringing the running total to 9 (ch3: 2, ch4: 1, ch5: 1, ch7/CLV-22: ~1, ch9/CLV-23: 1, ch10: 3) — still inside the §8.7 cap of ~13, but wasteful of budget and semantically misleading. A three-column TrackDiagram variant is ruled out by CLV-21.json out_of_scope[1], which prohibits modifying existing components unless a Spike surfaces a blocking issue; TrackDiagram.astro (site/src/components/TrackDiagram.astro, lines 5–16 and 40–46) hardcodes grid-template-columns: 1fr 80px 1fr for exactly two tracks with a FlowArrow centre column. Ch10's current content (site/src/content/guide/10-failure-handling.mdx, lines 9–25) presents three labelled subsections each with a compact 'Handling:' response description — the natural visual shape is three labelled lanes rendered side-by-side (desktop) or stacked (mobile), with each lane containing a category label, a one-line response description, and an escalation-destination badge. Ch5 (site/src/content/guide/05-delivery.mdx, lines 40–43) already lists the same three failure types in prose, confirming that a dedicated visual in ch10 is warranted. The diagram budget after CLV-22 and CLV-23 completions is approximately 6 (ch3: 2 + ch4: 1 + ch5: 1 + ch7: 1 + ch9: 1); a single composite for ch10 raises it to 7, well within the cap. The primitives FloatingLegend, Callout, and simple div-based grid are all available for reuse without touching existing components.
recommendation: Create a new FailureLanes component at site/src/components/FailureLanes.astro. It should render three labelled lanes in a CSS grid (grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr on desktop, collapsing to a single column below ~480px via a @media breakpoint, consistent with the mobile guidance being established by CLV-25). Each lane contains: a category label in the track-label monospace style (mechanical / quality / strategic), a brief response-shape description as body text, and a small badge indicating the escalation destination (same agent / Implementer / Discovery). FloatingLegend can be omitted (no agent/gate distinction needed) or replaced with a minimal inline legend explaining badge meaning. The component uses the same surface/border/accent token vocabulary as SingleTrack and TrackDiagram, counts as one diagram in the budget, and is entirely self-contained — no FlowArrow, no StepRow/StepArrow (categories are not pipeline steps). Estimated size is ~60–80 lines, comparable to TrackDiagram. The RFC out_of_scope clause is respected: no existing component is modified.
